hero.title: Coordinating Enterprise Analytics
hero.subtitle: An architectural perspective on semantic consistency, governance and modernization
hero.heading: Enterprise Data Architecture

problem.title: Enterprise analytics rarely fail because of technology.
problem.subtitle: They fail because organizations lose control over meaning.
list: As organizations grow, analytical capabilities evolve independently.
problem.message: Architecture exists to coordinate meaning before systems coordinate data.
sapPerspective: The same challenge appears during SAP modernization initiatives involving BW, Datasphere and Business Data Cloud, but it is fundamentally an enterprise architecture problem rather than a product problem.

thesis.title: Architectural coordination comes before platform selection.
thesis.subtitle: Every analytical architecture should answer four questions before selecting technology.

list.text: Which analytical assets should become reusable?

thesis.message: Good architecture makes organizational decisions explicit before technical decisions become permanent.
sapPerspective: Capabilities such as Business Data Cloud, Datasphere and Data Products deliver greater value when architectural decisions already exist.

evidence.title: Architecture proves itself through organizational permanence.

cards.title: SAP Global Template with Local Adaptations
cards.description: Nine Latin American countries running the same regional Data Analytics system, sharing data definitions.

cards.title: Self-Service Analytics Architecture
cards.description: Field teams needed off-line access to customer and sales data.

cards.title: System Decommissioning with Business Continuity
cards.description: Data Analytics environments had to be decommissioned while preserving historical business knowledge.

sapPerspective: Although implemented in SAP environments, these architectural decisions are platform-independent and applicable across enterprise analytics ecosystems.

architecture.title: Modern technology increases architectural leverage.
architecture.subtitle: Architectural responsibility remains essential.

relationship.meaning: Modern technology increases the leverage of architectural decisions.

architecture.message: Modern technology increases architectural leverage. It does not eliminate architectural responsibility.
sapPerspective: SAP Business Data Cloud, Datasphere and SAP Analytics Cloud strengthen governed analytical assets, semantic reuse and business ownership—but none replaces enterprise architecture.

value.title: Enabling sustainable modernization.
value.subtitle: Organizations rarely need another implementation.

nodes.title: Structure
nodes.description: Design enterprise analytical operating models and strengthen governance across distributed organizations.

nodes.title: Semantics
nodes.description: Establish shared definitions, reduce semantic fragmentation, and transform local assets into enterprise-wide capabilities.

nodes.title: Evolution
nodes.description: Connect legacy investments to modern platforms through clear roadmaps and architectural decisions.

value.message: Technology modernization succeeds only when organizational architecture evolves at the same pace.
sapPerspective: Equally applicable to SAP and non-SAP ecosystems, including hybrid environments combining Business Data Cloud, Datasphere and third-party analytical platforms.

pillars.title: Architectural Governance
pillars.description: Define and strengthen the governance structures that keep analytics aligned with business strategy.

pillars.title: Semantic Coordination
pillars.description: Reduce fragmentation and establish shared meaning across business units and analytical platforms.

pillars.title: Modernization Roadmaps
pillars.description: Connect legacy investments to modern platforms through clear, actionable architectural planning.

sapPerspective: Modernization programs benefit from structured semantic analysis and KPI harmonization as a prerequisite for a clean core.
Data Products and semantic layers are defined within the architecture before platforms are selected.
Hybrid analytics environments bridge SAP and non-SAP tools through shared definitions that enable self-service analytics without sacrificing governance.
